speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)

Mm-hmm. Let me turn to you, Ed Rogers. From the other side of the debate.

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)
text: It's been fun to watch.
Exactly. Republicans look at this and say, woo-woo!

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)
text: Yeah, more of the same out of the two frontrunners on the Democrat side would be good. I mean, this was sort of uncalled for. It was sloppy on both sides, didn't particularly flatter anyone. speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)

Mm-hmm. Now when you say this was deliberate, every campaign, as far as I understand it, has a squadron of people out looking for everything anybody says about them so they can respond to it quickly, correct?

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)
text: Sure. And in this case, they've both got good people. Now I do think you had a unique fusion of - The New York Times is where this was published.
Right.

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)
text: And you combine that with the power and the sort of how interesting it is that it was Geffen - a Bigfoot in Hollywood - and then you have a story that the other news media want to repeat, want to react to, etc., etc.

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)
text: So if this would have happened with some county chairman someplace being reported in Seattle, well, it never would've been any news at all. speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)
text: I think the larger issue is that primaries are very difficult, not just presidential, all primaries. There's real differences on policy and a whole range of issues, but in primaries, there tend to be, you know, many fewer differences among the candidates.

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)
text: So they're sizing each other up and trying to figure out how in terms of style, in terms of the issues I talk about, how I present myself. How am I going to differentiate myself? That's what they're trying to do now. It's a little early. That's why probably this was sort of surprising.

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)
text: It's a little early for them to start thinking about how am I going to go after the other candidates. We've got 10 months. speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)

speaker_label: Mr. ED ROGERS (Republican Strategist; Chairman, Barbour Griffith & Rogers)

speaker_label: Ms. ANNA GREENBERG (Democratic Strategist; Partner, Greenberg, Quinlan, & Rosner)
